title: Canonical derived scalar restriction compositors
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with topology $J$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For commutative ring sheaves $A,B,D$ on it let $\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ be the category of sheaves of modules over the underlying ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and use ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in a universe admitting these categories. For $f:A\to B$, define $\operatorname{res}_f:\operatorname{Mod}(B)\to\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ by restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $\operatorname{Res}_f=D(\operatorname{res}_f)$ by termwise restriction localized at quasi-isomorphisms. For $g:B\to D$, $h:A\to D$ and an equality $g f=h$, define the ordinary comparison $c_{f,g,h}:\operatorname{res}_g\operatorname{res}_f\cong\operatorname{res}_h$ (functor composition in diagrammatic order) to be the unique comparison whose component is the identity on every underlying module section. Define its derived comparison $\operatorname{Res}_g\operatorname{Res}_f\cong\operatorname{Res}_h$ by the canonical derived-composition isomorphism followed by the derived natural isomorphism of $c_{f,g,h}$. Define $\operatorname{Res}_{1_A}\cong 1_{D(\operatorname{Mod}(A))}$ by deriving the ordinary identity comparison and using the canonical derived-identity isomorphism.
